 J U D G M E N T
This claim petition is filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .10,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him in the accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief:-
On 21.05.2023 at about 10.45 a.m., the petitioner was travelling in Auto rickshaw bearing Regn.No.KA- 42-9671, in order to meet his father in law at Koornahosahalli to Sugatur and when he reached near Huladenahalli Govt Hospital, Huladenahalli Village, Tekal Hobli, Kolar Taluk, Kolar, said auto rickshaw driver drove the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and lost control over the vehicle and suddenly fell down.

Due to the accident, petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries and thereafter he was shifted to SNR Govt. Hospital and then to Gaurav Hospital, Kolar,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was working in Mahendra Aerospace Pvt Ltd., as an Associate and earning a sum of .47,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, the petitioner suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of auto by its driver.
The respondents, being the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. In pursuance of service of notice, 1st respondent appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
Respondent No.2 not appeared before the Tribunal and hence, he has been placed ex-parte.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.1 has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.1 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further, respondent No.1 contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further respondent No.2 denied for having insured the auto and the policy is standing in the previous owner name not got transferred in new owner name and the liability, if any, is subject to the terms and conditions of policy.
Further contended that the alleged auto was being driven by its driver without possessing valid and effective driving license, the auto was having no permit and FC as on the date of alleged accident.
Further the injured had also contributed to cause of alleged accident and was guilty of contributory negligence.
Further contended that the driver of auto suddenly applied the break and fell down, due to which petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

The materials placed on record disclose that the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective permit at the time of accident.
There is violation of terms and conditions of the policy of insurance as the vehicle has plied without valid permit.
As there is violation of conditions related to permit, the said violation falls under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
As per Sec.150 of M.V.Act, the insurance company can plead the defence related to violation of permit among other grounds provided under the said provision.
The materials on record clearly disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit as well as conditions of policy of insurance by respondent No.2.
It is pertinent to note that respondent No.2 not appeared before the tribunal and also not placed any materials in order to negate the contention of respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2, being owner of the vehicle, is proper person to state about existence of permit and its validity at the time of accident.
But, respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed materials to show the aspect of existence of permit or its validity at the time of accident.
Respondent No.2 not placed materials to show that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective permit as on the date of accident.
The materials placed on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms and conditions of policy by respondent No.2 related to permit.
24. The accident in question occurred on 21.05.2023 i.e., subsequent to the amendment which came into effect from 1/4/2022.

By virtue of amendment, S 149(4) of old IMV Act, which provided the principle of pay and recover, has been deleted and the provision similar to S 149(4) of IMV Act has not been inserted in amended provision of S 150 of IMV Act.
The principle of pay and recover has been provided in S 149(4) of old Act and said principle has not been provided in S 150 of IMV Act.

Though the nature of violations of terms of policy has been stated in S 149 of IMV Act prior to amendment as well as S 150 of IMV Act subsequent to amendment, the provision for pay and recover has not been inserted in amended provision of S 150 of IMV Act.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.
In the present case, the Offending vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-42-9671 does not appear to have valid permit at the time of accident which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.

Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of conditions of permit, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

Further, in view of the amendment to the Act, as discussed supra, no liability can be fastened on Respondent No.1, to pay the compensation and to recover the same from the Respondent No.2 under pay and recovery theory.

sentences.text: Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioner is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by plying the vehicle without possessing valid and effective permit at the time of accident.
The offending vehicle does not have permit to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed any materials in order to controvert the contention of respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 not placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
Respondent No.2 not put forth any contention contrary to the version of respondent No.1.
There is violation of terms of the policy issued by respondent No.1.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.1 to pay the compensation.
Respondent No.2, being the owner of the auto, is liable to pay the compensation.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The respondent No.2 could have appeared before the Tribunal and denied the involvement of the vehicle or negligence of the driver in the cause of accident.
The owner of the auto is the proper and better person to state about involvement of the vehicle as well as negligence of the driver in the cause of accident.
But, the owner of the offending auto failed to appear before the Tribunal in spite of service of notice and not resisted the claim in any manner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondent not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The evidence of RW.1 clearly discloses that the offending auto was not having valid permit at the time of accident and evidence of the witness is substantiated by Ex.R.3.
discloses that the offending vehicle does not have valid and effective permit at the time of accident.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal to show the validity of permit or existence of permit as on the date of accident.
No materials are placed before the Tribunal in order to controvert the evidence of RW.1.
The materials placed on record disclose that the offending vehicle was not having valid and effective permit at the time of accident.
There is violation of terms and conditions of the policy of insurance as the vehicle has plied without valid permit.
As there is violation of conditions related to permit, the said violation falls under Sec.150 of M.V.Act.
As per Sec.150 of M.V.Act, the insurance company can plead the defence related to violation of permit among other grounds provided under the said provision.
The materials on record clearly disclose the aspect of violation of conditions of permit as well as conditions of policy of insurance by respondent No.2.
Respondent No.2, being owner of the vehicle, is proper person to state about existence of permit and its validity at the time of accident.
But, respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed materials to show the aspect of existence of permit or its validity at the time of accident.
Respondent No.2 not placed materials to show that the offending vehicle was having valid and effective permit as on the date of accident.
The materials placed on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms and conditions of policy by respondent No.2 related to permit.
By virtue of amendment, S 149(4) of old IMV Act, which provided the principle of pay and recover, has been deleted and the provision similar to S 149(4) of IMV Act has not been inserted in amended provision of S 150 of IMV Act.
The principle of pay and recover has been provided in S 149(4) of old Act and said principle has not been provided in S 150 of IMV Act.
Though the nature of violations of terms of policy has been stated in S 149 of IMV Act prior to amendment as well as S 150 of IMV Act subsequent to amendment, the provision for pay and recover has not been inserted in amended provision of S 150 of IMV Act.
As per the provisions of Sec.150 of Motor Vehicles, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability to pay compensation if there is violation of terms of the policy.
In the present case, the Offending vehicle bearing Regn.No.KA-42-9671 does not appear to have valid permit at the time of accident which aspect is forthcoming from the materials placed on record.
The materials on record disclose the aspect of violation of terms of the policy.
Though the policy pertaining to offending vehicle is in existence at the time of accident, as there is violation of conditions of permit, the insurance company cannot be held liable to pay the compensation.

10 25.
Accordingly, the Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the liability of paying the compensation to the petitioner is to be fastened solely on the Respondent No.2, who is the owner of the offending vehicle, as he has violated the policy condition by plying the vehicle without possessing valid and effective permit at the time of accident.
The offending vehicle does not have permit to ply the vehicle as on the date of accident.
Respondent No.2 neither appeared nor placed any materials in order to controvert the contention of respondent No.1.
Respondent No.2 not placed materials to show that the vehicle involved in the accident was taken without his permission or knowledge.
As there is violation of terms of the policy, the liability cannot be fastened on respondent No.1 to pay the compensation.
